stories.title: This Blue Whale Population Grew 1,000% Since the End of Antarctic Whaling
stories.label: ocean
stories.summary: Antarctic blue whales, the largest animals ever to live on Earth, have made an astonishing comeback. Their numbers have grown from just 418 whales to about 4,018 since 1973, an increase of roughly 1,000%. That works out to steady growth of about 4.5% every year. The recovery followed the end of Antarctic whaling, and it shows that when people stop harming a species and protect it, nature can bounce back.
stories.why_good: A real, measured recovery of the planet's largest animal, driven by human protection that actually worked.

stories.title: West Coast's First Ever Sea Turtle Hatchlings Released into the Pacific
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Back in late September, a female olive ridley sea turtle came ashore on a California beach, dug a nest, and laid her eggs before slipping back into the sea. When a storm approached, people stepped in to protect the eggs, and the hatchlings were saved. Over the weekend, the baby turtles were released into the Pacific Ocean. It's the first time sea turtle hatchlings have ever been released on the West Coast.
stories.why_good: A rare, first-of-its-kind success for a sea turtle species, with tiny hatchlings now swimming free in the Pacific.
